source_text: Μεταμόρφωσις ἀνθρώποις μεμυθολόγηται· μεταμορφοῦνται δὲ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν καὶ οἱ θεοί.Δένδρον ἡ Ῥέα γίνεται, δράκων δὲ ὁ Ζεὺς διὰ τὴν Φερσέφατταν, αἴγειροι αἱ τοῦ Φαέθοντος ἀδελφαί, καὶ ἡ Λητὼ ζῶον εὐτελές, δι᾿ ἣν Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται. Θεὸς εἰπέ μοι κύκνος γίνεται, καὶ τὴν ἀετοῦ μορφὴν ἀναλαμβάνει, καὶ δι᾿ οἰνοχοΐαν τοῦ Γανυμήδους τῇ παιδεραστίᾳ σεμνύνεται; Τί μοι σέβειν θεοὺς δωρολήπτας, καὶ ὀργιζομένους ἂν μὴ λάβωσιν; Ἐχέτωσαν οὗτοι τὴν εἱμαρμένην· τοὺς πλανήτας προσκυνεῖν οὐ βούλομαι. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ Βερενίκης πλόκαμος; Ποῦ δὲ οἱ ἀστέρες αὐτῆς πρὶν τὴν προειρημένην ἀποθανεῖν; Πῶς δὲ ὁ τεθνεὼς Ἀντίνοος μειράκιον ἐν τῇ σελήνῃ ὡραῖον καθίδρυται; Τίς ὁ ἀναβιβάσας αὐτόν, εἰ μή τις καὶ τοῦτον, ὡς τοὺς βασιλέας μισθοῦ δι᾿ ἐπιορκίας τις, τοὺς θεοὺς καταγελῶν, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι φήσας πεπίστευται, κατὰ τὸ ὅμοιον θεολογήσας τιμῆς καὶ δωρεᾶς ἠξίωται; Τί μοι τὸν θεον σεσυλήκατε; Τί δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν ποίησιν ἀτιμάζετε; Θύεις πρόβατον, τὸ δ᾿ αὐτὸ προσκυνεῖς· ταῦρός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα σφάττεις αὐτοῦ. Ζῶον πονηρὸν ὁ ἐνγόνασι ἐκθλίβει· καὶ τὸν ἀνθρωποποιὸν Προμηθία καταφαγών ἀετὸς τετίμηται.Καλὸς ὁ κύκνος, ὅτι μοιχὸς ἦν· καλοὶ δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑτεροήμεροι Διόσκουροι, τῶν Λευκιππίδων οἱ ἁρπασταί. Κρείττων ἡ Ἑλένη, τὸν μὲν καρήξανθον Μενέλαον καταλιποῦσα, τῷ δὲ μιτρηφόρῳ καὶ πολυχρύσῳ Πάριδι κατακολουθοῦσα. Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων, ὁ τὴν ἐκπορνεύσασαν εἰς Ἠλύσια πεδία μετατεθεικώς. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἡ Τυνδαρὶς ἀπηθανάτισται· καὶ σοφῶς ὁ Εὐριπίδης ὑπὸ Ὀρέστου τῆς προειρημένης γυναικὸς τὴν ἀναίρεσιν παρεισήγαγε.
pass_a_gloss: Transformation is mythologized for humans; but your gods also are transformed. The Rhea becomes a tree, and Zeus becomes a serpent through Persephone, and the sisters of Phaethon become goats, and Leto becomes a lowly animal, because of which Delos is now called Ortygia. Tell me, does God become a swan, and take on the form of an eagle, and is he honored because of the wine-pouring of Ganymede and his pederasty? Why should I reverence gods who are bribed and become angry if they do not receive? Let them have their fate; I do not wish to worship the planets. What is the hair of Berenice? And where are her stars before the aforementioned woman died? And how is the dead Antinous, a beautiful youth, established in the moon? Who has brought him up, if not someone who, like the kings for a fee through perjury, mocking the gods, has said that he has gone up into heaven, and has been deemed worthy of honor and gift according to the same theology? What have you plundered from God? And why do you dishonor his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, and yet you worship the same thing; a bull is in heaven, and you slaughter its image. A wicked animal, the eagle, tears to pieces; and the eagle that devoured the creator Prometheus is honored. The swan is beautiful because it was an adulterer; and the Dioscuri, the abductors of the Leucippides, are beautiful. Helen is better, having left the feeble Menelaus and having followed the mitre-phoros and rich Paris. Lycaon and Socrates, who transferred the prostitute to the Elysian fields. But not even Tyndareus has been deified; and wisely Euripides introduced the destruction of the aforementioned woman by Orestes.
pass_b_english: The idea of transformation is often mythologized in human stories, but it's also a common theme with your gods. For instance, Rhea turns into a tree, and Zeus becomes a serpent through his connection to Persephone. Similarly, the sisters of Phaethon are transformed into goats, and Leto becomes a lowly animal - which is why Delos is now known as Ortygia. Can God really take on different forms, like a swan or an eagle, and be revered for his involvement with Ganymede and his pederastic relationships? Why should I worship gods who can be bribed and get angry if they don't receive offerings? Let them have their fate, but I refuse to worship the planets. What's the significance of Berenice's hair, and where were her stars before she died? How did the deceased Antinous, a beautiful young man, end up being established in the moon? Who could have possibly elevated him to such a status, if not someone who, like corrupt kings, lied under oath and mocked the gods, claiming he had ascended to heaven and deserved honor and gifts? What have you taken from God, and why do you disrespect his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, yet you worship the same creature; there's a bull in heaven, but you slaughter its image on earth. It's ironic that the eagle, a wicked animal, is honored for tearing things apart, and the eagle that devoured Prometheus, the creator, is revered. The swan is admired for its adulterous ways, and the Dioscuri, who abducted the Leucippides, are also praised. Helen is often considered better than others, having left her weak husband Menelaus to follow the wealthy and attractive Paris. Even figures like Lycaon and Socrates, who helped a prostitute reach the Elysian fields, are notable. However, not even Tyndareus has been deified, and Euripides wisely portrayed the demise of the aforementioned woman at the hands of Orestes. The contradictions and flaws in these mythological stories raise important questions about the nature of God and worship.

review.notes: Pass B adds significant interpretive commentary and summary at the end that is not in the Greek source: 'The contradictions and flaws in these mythological stories raise important questions about the nature of God and worship.' Furthermore, Pass A contains a mistranslation of 'Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων' as 'Lycaon and Socrates'; the Greek refers to Lycaon and Sophron (proper names), whereas Socrates is a different figure entirely. Pass B also translates 'Σώφρων' as 'Socrates'.
reasons: Pass B adds a concluding sentence 'The contradictions and flaws in these mythological stories raise important questions about the nature of God and worship.' which is not present in the Greek source.

Pass A and B both fail on the translation of 'Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων': Pass A translates it as 'Lycaon and Socrates' and Pass B as 'Lycaon and Socrates', but the Greek 'Σώφρων' is the name Sophron, not Socrates.
